title: verified-circuits: kernel-checkable mechanistic circuits for learned transformers
description:
A tiny transformer is trained from scratch on a complete finite task — Dyck-1 balanced parentheses over every input up to length 16 — reverse-engineered into a human-readable symbolic circuit, and shipped with independently checkable evidence that Spec == Circuit == Model over the entire input domain.

The chain is three links at three named trust levels. Circuit == Spec is a Lean 4 theorem proved by structural induction, so it holds for every length; the axiom audit reports only propext and Quot.sound (no sorry, no native_decide, no Mathlib), so a sceptic trusts only the Lean kernel. Circuit == Model is a rigorous interval-arithmetic certificate over exact dyadic rationals with outward rounding, giving a strictly positive decision margin on every one of the 65,536 inputs at n=16 (rational margin lower bound ≥ +8.0950), re-verifiable from the weight export alone by a torch-free checker. The remaining seam — that the Lean and Python definitions transcribe the same algorithm — is corroborated, not proven, and is labelled as such.

The model is deliberately tiny and the task deliberately simple. The contribution is not scale: it is the complete, checkable chain from specification to circuit to trained weights, with each link's trust level named.

This is the first repository of three. It is continued by certified-grokking, which applies the same discipline to a canonical checkpoint the authors did not train, and by certified-inference, which carries it to a real pretrained LayerNorm language model too large to enumerate.

This record archives the repository as of 11 August 2026. The work was first made public on 14 June 2026; the DOI was minted later, so the archive date and the original publication date differ.
